algorithm-design-manual:1-30.title: The two TSP heuristics from Section 1.1
algorithm-design-manual:1-30.source: The Algorithm Design Manual, Section 1.1, p. 5
algorithm-design-manual:1-30.content:
## 1. Nearest-neighbor heuristic

Start at an arbitrary point. Repeatedly travel to the closest point that has not been visited yet. Once every point has been visited, return to the starting point to close the tour.

```text
NearestNeighbor(P)
    choose a starting point p0
    tour = [p0]
    current = p0

    while there is an unvisited point:
        next = closest unvisited point to current
        append next to tour
        current = next

    append p0 to tour
    return tour
```

It is easy and fast to implement, but the early greedy choices can leave an unnecessarily long final connection.

## 2. Closest-pair heuristic

Initially, treat every point as a one-point chain. Repeatedly connect the closest pair of chain endpoints, subject to two constraints: no point may receive more than two tour edges, and the connection may not create a cycle before all points have been joined. Merge the chains after each accepted connection. When one chain contains every point, connect its two remaining endpoints to form the cycle.

```text
ClosestPair(P)
    make each point its own chain
    while more than one chain remains:
        choose the shortest endpoint-to-endpoint connection
            that does not give a point degree greater than 2
            and does not close a cycle early
        add the connection
        merge the two chains

    connect the two endpoints of the final chain
    return the resulting tour
```

## What to measure

Implement both heuristics, run them on the same point sets, and compare **tour length**, not just runtime. For a fair experiment, use several fixed and randomized instances, use the same starting-point policy for nearest neighbor, and report the average and best tour lengths. A useful extension is to run 2-opt on the shorter initial tour: replace two nonadjacent edges with the other reconnection when it shortens the tour, reversing the intervening segment so the result remains a valid cycle.
